expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: "> **Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**" is the first line

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: The briefing has four bold headings: "**Key debates**", "**Major voices**", "**Patterns**", "**Open questions**"

expectations.text: The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: Estimated at about 370 words across the four sections, which is within 300–500

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "I saved an interactive map in your folder: `.../mind-map.html`". The file uses the template's DATA structure, and the template was read this session.

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: The reply lists six angles. Each top-level branch visible in the shortened file has 3 children, and every visible node has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (e.g. "saturation": 0.78, 0.5, 0.3). The file is cut off, so the remaining branches could not be checked.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: Labels are short topics, e.g. "Academic achievement", "Perceptions vs. measured outcomes", "Off-day programs that offset savings". Questions appear only in separate "questions" fields.

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: The reply only asks "which angle draws you in" and never recommends one

expectations.text: Every link or DOI that appears in the reply or the mind map points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: Every visible link (nwea.org, PMC9979633, the74million, edweek 2026/04, chalkbeat, edweek 2023/02, PMC8595551) appears in the WebFetch log. The rest of the mind map file is cut off and could not be checked.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "which angle draws you in, and what makes it worth researching beyond 'it's interesting'?"

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: Only the closing compound question is addressed to the user. The briefing's open questions are about the topic, and "You can also ask me..." is not a question.
